body:
`R/scm.R` reports **0.0% coverage** — the lowest in the package by a wide margin, against 86.7% overall.

```
   0.0%  R/scm.R
  51.4%  R/legacy.R
  86.0%  R/analysis_class.R
  ...
 100.0%  R/ec_weights.R, R/method_class.R, R/run_analysis.R, ...
```

## It is not actually untested — but it is under-tested and unverified where it matters

Both scm tests are guarded by `skip_on_cran()`:

- `tests/testthat/test-full_pipeline_scm.R:4`
- `tests/testthat/test-run_analysis.R:127`

`skip_on_cran()` skips unless `NOT_CRAN` is `"true"`. That gives three different behaviours:

| Environment | `NOT_CRAN` | scm tests |
|---|---|---|
| local `devtools::test()` | `true` | **run** (PASS 6) |
| GitHub Actions | `true` (set by r-lib/actions) | **run** |
| `covr::package_coverage()` | unset | **skipped** → 0% |
| CRAN | unset | **skipped** |

So the 0% is a coverage-reporting artifact, not a claim that nothing exercises `scm()`. Two real problems remain.

## 1. Never verified on CRAN's machines

`scm()` depends on `CVXR`, and CVXR depends on a solver whose behaviour varies by platform and build. A CRAN-only failure in the SCM path would not be caught by any check we run — which is not hypothetical: a CVXR macOS binary issue took out CI for every PR on 2026-09-22 (#73).

The guard exists for a real reason (the unguarded `scm(bootstrap = 50)` test was the main cause of the 10-minute CRAN check timeout that got 0.0.4.0 rejected). The fix is not to remove it, but to add a cheap CRAN-safe smoke test alongside it — a single small solve, no bootstrap, asserting shape and finiteness rather than locked values.

## 2. The test itself is thin

The one full-pipeline test pins a single configuration:

```r
scm(lambda_min = 0.0005, lambda_max = 0.0005, nlambda = 1,
    bootstrap = 10, bootstrap_ci_type = "perc")
```

That is `nlambda = 1` with `lambda_min == lambda_max`, i.e. the degenerate case with no lambda path to search. None of these are exercised:

- `nlambda > 1` with a real `lambda_min` < `lambda_max` range — the actual regularisation-path code
- the package defaults (`lambda_min = 0`, `lambda_max = 0.1`, `nlambda = 2L`, `bootstrap = 200L`)
- `parallel = "multicore"` / `"snow"`, `ncpus > 1`
- `bootstrap_ci_type` other than `"perc"` (see #77 — three of the five accepted values were broken precisely because only `"perc"` was ever tested)

This is the same argument-value coverage gap behind #71 and #77: the lines execute, but never with the argument values that would break them. Line coverage cannot see it.

## Suggested work

1. Add a CRAN-safe smoke test for `scm()` — small, no bootstrap, shape and finiteness only — so the SCM path is exercised on CRAN without reintroducing the timeout.
2. Add a test with `nlambda > 1` over a real lambda range, so the path-search code is covered.
3. Decide whether covr should run with `NOT_CRAN=true` so reported coverage reflects what the suite actually tests. Note there is currently no codecov workflow, so nothing publishes this number today.
title: scm() reports 0% coverage and is never verified on CRAN
